I am a statistical consultant at the University of Melbourne [Statistical Consulting Centre (SCC)](https://scc.ms.unimelb.edu.au/), where I've worked since 2017. This involves working with researchers at the University and clients outside the University. We can assist with all stages of quantitative research: designing experiments or surveys, planning an appropriate analysis, analysing data, making graphs and communicating results clearly in papers or reports. As part of my role at the SCC, I also teach two short courses [Introduction to R and Reproducible Research](https://scc.ms.unimelb.edu.au/training/introduction-to-r-and-reproducible-research), alongside Dr Sandy Clarke-Errey; and [Mixed Models in R](https://scc.ms.unimelb.edu.au/training/mixed-models-in-r), alongside Dr Jeremy Silver.

I recently completed a research Masters degree at the [Clinical Epidemiology & Biostatistics Unit (CEBU)](https://www.mcri.edu.au/research/research-areas/population-health/clinical-epidemiology-biostatistics-cebu) of the Murdoch Children's Research Institute in Melbourne, Australia. My research was about estimating complier average causal effects (CACE) in clinical trials with missing compliance data, supervised by [Professor Katherine Lee](https://www.mcri.edu.au/researcher-details/katherine-lee), [Professor Margarita Moreno-Betancur](https://www.mcri.edu.au/researcher-details/margarita-moreno-betancur) and [Associate Professor Thomas Sullivan](https://research.sahmri.org.au/en/persons/thomas-sullivan).

I served on the [Statistical Society of Australia](https://statsoc.org.au/) Victoria and Tasmania Branch Council from 2021--2024.

You can find me [on Bluesky](https://bsky.app/profile/cameronpat.bsky.social) or email me at cameron.patrick@unimelb.edu.au
